title: Precision Neuromodulation for Chronic Pain: Integrating Functional MRI and Focused Ultrasound for Personalised Treatment
summary: This study aims to use functional MRI to identify brain areas involved in pain processing and target them individually using focused ultrasound. Three conditions (conventional, personalized, and placebo stimulation) will be compared. Effectiveness will be measured by pain scales and brain scans.

interventions.name: A conventional FUS stimulation targeting a common region (e.g., the anterior insula)
A personalized FUS stimulation tailored to the individual cortical pain signatures of each patient.
A sham stimulation serving as a placebo control. All procedures of the active stimulation (e.g., neuronavigation, gel application) are performed, but no active FUS is applied.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of chronic low back pain according to IASP criteria (>6 months duration)
- Moderate to severe pain intensity (NRS)
- Stable pain medication for at least 4 weeks
- MRI compatibility
- Neurological assessment without relevant findings
- Ability to provide informed consent
- Sufficient language and cognitive skills
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 or >60
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Severe neurological or psychiatric disorders
- MRI contraindications
- Unstable medical conditions
- Recent participation in other studies
- Unstable pain medication
- Inability to provide consent
- Ongoing unstable pain therapy or alternative treatments
